During the motion, the wooden board always remains horizontal, and the block always remains stationary relative to the wooden board. Then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: From b to a, the block is in an overweight state.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a dashed circle. The two ends of the horizontal dashed diameter are labeled b and a, with b at the left end and a at the right end; the upper and lower ends of the vertical dashed diameter are respectively labeled c and d, with c at the upper end and d at the lower end. In the figure, near positions a and b, small wooden boards kept horizontal and the blocks on them are drawn, indicating that the board and the block move in circular motion in a vertical plane. The problem statement says that the direction of motion is counterclockwise, and that the board is always horizontal and the block is stationary relative to the board. Reasoning: The block undergoes uniform circular motion with the board, so the centripetal acceleration at any point points toward the center of the circle. When the board is horizontal, the supporting force of the board on the block is vertically upward, and gravity is vertically downward; if the block has an upward vertical acceleration component, then N - mg > 0, that is, the supporting force N is greater than gravity mg, and the block is in an overweight state. In the lower half of the circle, in the counterclockwise direction from b through d to a, the center of the circle is above the block, and the centripetal acceleration has a vertically upward component, so the block is overweight; in the upper semicircle, the centripetal acceleration has a downward component, and the block is weightless. Therefore, the overweight process is the motion process along the lower semicircle from b to a.
